subject: Categorical outcome AIC value cannot be obatained

messages.author: 05098db296c21f01
messages.subject: Categorical outcome AIC value cannot be obatained
parts:
Hi,
This may be a simple question. I'm beginner and want to understand this correctly I'm developing a sem for categorical outcome. AIC of the model cannot be calculated as the estimator is not ML. I get a warning that " lavaan WARNING: logLik only available if estimator is ML". Could someone explain this to me? is there anyother way to find AIC value for the model?

Thank you in advance

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Categorical outcome AIC value cannot be obatained
parts: Could someone explain this to me? is there anyother way to find AIC value for the model?

Information criteria are a function of likelihoods used during estimation.  Least-squares estimators do not employ likelihoods, so there is no basis for calculating them (except in much simpler regression models, because OLS estimates are in fact ML estimates in those cases).

You could try using pairwise ML estimation instead of the default DWLS (set estimator = "PML").  AIC will be available only from a hidden function:  https://groups.google.com/g/lavaan/c/jwh4hRdTdnc/m/SNPfPGbXAQAJ

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.subject: Re: Categorical outcome AIC value cannot be obatained
parts: I tried PML estimator. Does it only work with two ot more categorical variables? Because i get an error "at least two categorical variables are needed"

I wasn't aware of that limitation, but that is what the message clearly says.  I suppose you could generate a random dummy code to add to your model as an additional outcome.  Obviously you aren't interested in it, but you could then use PML to get AIC.
